newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The welfare and population development ministry would launch an ambitious project to reregister South Africa's three million social welfare grant beneficiaries in a bid to stop abuse of the system, Welfare Minister Geraldine Fraser Moleketi said on Sunday.
- The Presidential Review Commission responsible for investigating government restructuring and service delivery - reprimanded the finance department on Sunday for treating the commission shoddily.

- Government could receive up to two billion rand over the next year from the sale of several state assets, notably the Airports Company, finance department deputy director-general Andre Roux said at the weekend.

- A critical report by consultants on the proposed rationalisation of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) has made far-reaching proposals, calling for an overhaul of the SADC's institutions and operations.

- African National Congress Gauteng MP Oupa Monareng, who was convicted of attempting to bribe a policeman, would not be expelled from the provincial legislature but would be "redeployed" from the safety and security standing committee, sources said at the weekend.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Investors in stainless steel tank containers would be allowed to keep offshore any profit generated from the investment, Richard Eaton, a director of Multistar Container Transport, said last week.

- Coca-Cola South Africa (CCSA) had embarked on a drastic restructuring programme to prepare the company to be run by black South Africans over the next three years, company spokesmen said at the weekend.

- The Industrial Development Corporation (IDC), the country's development financier, is considering bringing black economic empowerment groups on board as co-partners in its various multibillion-rand benefication projects, Gert Gouws, the general manager for finance, said at the weekend.

- Panicky late rand trade in the face of a rampant dollar on Friday resulted in the local currency losing almost 3 cents of its value to fall to a six-and-a-half month low of 4,6345 rand, traders said at the weekend.

- European Union officials have announced only a quarter of last year's EU aid budget for South Africa was actually paid out - 150 million rand was handed over out of an annual total budget of 616 million rand.
SAKE BEELD
- The government is claiming 252 million rand from East Rand Proprietary Mines (ERPM) , one of South Africa's best known gold mines, for a loan it granted to the company in the 1980's.
- Whitey (James Wellwood) Bason, general director of Shoprite Checkers was on Friday chosen as (newspaper) Die Burger's business leader of the year.
THE STAR
- Council paypoints were quiet last week, but business is expected to pick up from today as residents rush to pay outstanding bills ahead of tomorrow's planned electricity switchoff.
- The recent spate of killings in the Richmond area in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands is related to a third-force network, President Nelson Mandela said on Sunday.

- Organised business and labour are set to collide today as the Congress of SA Trade Unions flexes its muscles to press home demands around the draft Basic Conditions of Employment Bill after failed attempts to broker a settlement.
- More than 25,000 policemen will embark on various forms of labour action this week in protet against the proposed 7.5 percent salary increase, according to the South African Police Union.
